summary: Intermittent protobuf-framed messages split across websocket chunks causing partial outputs and failed resume
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Noteable Labs) reports intermittent truncated responses and failed resume when using our websocket streaming API with a protobuf-framed binary payload inside websocket messages. The customer is using a long-lived websocket to stream token deltas encoded in protobuf messages. When a reconnect occurs, their client attempts to resume from the last received sequence id, but occasionally the server/consumer sees a partially-framed protobuf message (missing trailing bytes), causing the resume handshake to fail or produce corrupted partial text in the final output.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-visible truncation or garbled tokens in final fragments for ~2% of streams during heavy traffic spikes.
- Automated retries by the customer's SDK sometimes produce duplicate partial tokens or fail to resume, prompting application-level confusion and dropped transcripts.
- Affects dedicated customers in us-west with specific proxy topology.

Environment:
- Customer dedicated instance hosted in us-west-2, running on Dedicated cluster D-17.
- Client SDK: noteable-rt-stream v1.3.2 (uses protobuf framing: varint length prefix + proto message).
- Edge proxy: managed Envoy fleet with TLS termination -> websocket proxying -> websocket-gateway.
- Redwood websocket gateway version: 2026.01.15.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Open long-lived websocket and start streaming a request that will produce ~500 tokens (model: open-instruct-3b-v1).
2) Simulate network blips (client-side short drop ~200-600ms) or cause backend scaling events.
3) Reconnect the websocket; client attempts resume with last-sequence-id.
4) Observe: sometimes resume fails with server reporting "invalid-frame" or the final chunk contains garbled text fragments.

Logs / evidence provided by customer:
- Websocket client logs with base64 of last 3 frames showing truncated protobuf payloads (attached in ticket).
- ts=2026-03-09T21:14:02Z gateway logs: "ws:incoming:frame_incomplete seq=4232 conn=ab12..." repeated for same connection id.
- tcpdump from customer side showing original frames intact when captured at customer edge but truncated after our proxy (suggests re-chunking or buffer sizing issue in transit).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged receipt of customer's logs and requested PCAP + sample base64 frames. Escalated to SRE for investigation of edge-proxy behavior.

2026-03-10 - Ethan Li (SRE): Captured websocket gateway traces for conn ab12...; observed occasional frame fragmentation where binary message length prefix claims more bytes than available in a single frame and we're buffering across frames — reassembly should handle this but appears to time out under backpressure.

2026-03-11 - Customer (Noteable Labs - Samir Gupta): Provided pcap captured at customer edge showing intact full frames; also shared that their SDK does strict length-prefixed decoding and fails fast on partial frames.

2026-03-11 - Ethan Li (SRE): Reproduced flaky behavior in staging by enabling high concurrency and injecting 200-800ms ephemeral latency on the edge proxy. Observed that our proxy's websocket frame coalescing disabled path re-emits partial frames to downstream handler rather than buffering until full message-length is available. Creating patch branch to change behavior.
2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Support): Notified customer that we have a hotfix pending and asked for permission to schedule a brief maintenance window for their dedicated cluster D-17 to apply the fix.
2026-03-12 - Samir Gupta (Customer): Approved maintenance window 2026-03-13 03:00-03:15 UTC. Customer requested post-fix verification steps and asks for a mitigation until patch is live.

2026-03-12 - Ethan Li (SRE): Suggested interim mitigation: enable websocket-level coarse buffering on the customer's dedicated edge proxy (routing flag: ws_buffer_mode=buffer_until_msg_complete) and increase connection read timeout to 2s to avoid timeouts on reassembly. Provided CLI command to toggle flag on D-17.
2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Support): Documented workaround and added step-by-step commands in ticket; awaiting customer's confirmation after toggling flag.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: partial protobuf messages are delivered to the websocket-gateway due to proxy re-chunking and a strict timeout in the gateway's reassembly logic leading to dropped trailing bytes.

Evidence: customer pcap shows full message lengths; intermediate proxy traces show segmentation at 16KB boundaries that do not align with protobuf length-prefixed boundaries. Gateway logs show 'frame_timeout' events at 200-600ms which coincide with network blip windows.

Repro: deterministically reproduced in staging by introducing artificial latency and limiting socket buffer to 8KB; confirms gateway times out and forwards incomplete payloads when reassembly path returns early.

Root cause (working theory): edge-proxy/Envoy config has 'ws_stream_buffer_limit' set to 8KB and short reassembly timeout; under backpressure the envoy breaks binary websocket frames into multiple underlying TCP writes and our gateway's reader does not block to recompose until full varint length decoded, leading to partial proto messages being processed as final frames.
resolution_notes: Hotfix created: edge-proxy patch changes websocket proxying to ensure message reassembly at proxy level or mark frames as continued to the gateway. PR: github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/812.

Gateway change: increased reassembly timeout to 2s and strengthened validation for length-prefixed protobuf frames — gateway will now hold partial fragments until full message length received or until new larger timeout expires.

Immediate mitigation (applied to D-17 on 2026-03-13 03:05 UTC): toggled ws_buffer_mode=buffer_until_msg_complete and increased read timeout; applied to customer's dedicated cluster. Customer confirmed that previously failing streams now complete without truncation in a follow-up test run (attachment: post-patch transcript).

Follow ups: schedule rollout of hotfix to shared websocket gateway fleet, update runbook to include checks for 'ws_buffer_mode' and buffer size thresholds, add automated smoke test that sends varint-length prefixed protobuf frames and induces transient latency to validate reassembly under load.
Customer communication: Maya Chen sent summary and post-fix verification report; customer asked for a postmortem which will be produced and linked to this ticket.
